en: 60 g fine vermicelli
2 eggs
1 tsp sugar, ground cardamom
Saffron threads, a little rose water
1 tsp ghee
Break the vermicelli into short pieces and toast in ghee 2 minutes
Add enough water and boil until cooked
Add the sugar, cardamom, saffron and rose water
Beat the egg and pour it over in a pan until it sets
1 khameer flatbread
40 g low-fat cottage cheese
1 tsp honey
Tomato and cucumber slices
Fresh thyme (optional)
Warm the khameer briefly in the oven or a pan
Spread the cheese over it
Arrange the tomato and cucumber on top
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle the thyme

name.en: Chebab (Gulf Sweet Pancakes with Date Syrup)

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Low-fat milk 120 ml
1 egg
Brown sugar 1 tsp and ground cardamom a pinch
Baking powder half a tsp and a pinch of saffron (optional)
Date syrup 2 tbsp to serve
Mix the flour with the milk, egg, brown sugar, cardamom, baking powder and saffron if desired until a smooth, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Let it rest 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan, pour two tablespoons of batter to form a small disc, cook 1-2 minutes on each side until golden.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stack the pancakes and drizzle with date syrup, and serve warm.

name.en: Regag Bread with Egg and Cheese

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g and water about 70 ml
1 egg
Low-fat grated cheese 30 g
A pinch of chopped spring onion
A little salt and a pinch of ground cumin
1 tsp oil
Mix the flour with the water gradually until a very thin, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour a very thin layer of batter to cover the base.
Cook for a minute until the edges dry, crack the egg over it and spread, sprinkle with the cheese, spring onion, salt and cumin.
Cover the pan and cook 2-3 minutes until the egg is cooked and the cheese melts, fold the edges inward and serve hot.

name.en: Aseeda (Wheat Flour Pudding with Date Syrup)

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g
Water 300 ml
Low-fat butter 1 tsp
A pinch of salt
Date syrup 2 tbsp to serve
A pinch of ground cardamom (optional)
Boil the water with the salt in a pot.
Sprinkle in the flour gradually while stirring quickly and continuously to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat and continue stirring 8-10 minutes until the texture becomes as cohesive as soft dough and starts pulling away from the sides of the pot.
Add the butter and stir, pour into a serving bowl, make a well in the centre and pour the date syrup into it, sprinkle with cardamom if desired and serve hot.

name.en: Ful Khaleeji (Gulf-Style Fava Beans with Tomato and Cumin)

en: Canned fava beans, drained, 200 g
Diced tomato and chopped onion
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin 1 tsp
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
Ragag or whole-wheat bread to serve (optional)
Place the drained fava beans in a small pot with a little water, cook over medium heat 5-7 minutes until heated through and some beans start to break down.
Mash half the beans lightly with a fork for a creamy texture while keeping some whole.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt and black pepper and stir.
Pour into a serving plate, drizzle with lemon juice and olive oil, arrange the tomato and onion on top, and serve with bread if desired.

name.en: Khubz Tandoor with Cheese and Za'atar

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 35 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Low-fat grated cheese 40 g
Dried thyme (zaatar) 1 tsp and 1 tsp olive oil
A pinch of salt
Nigella seeds a pinch for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast and salt gradually until a soft, cohesive dough forms, let it rest 30 minutes.
Roll into a medium-thickness circle on a lined tray.
Sprinkle with the cheese and thyme, drizzle with olive oil and nigella seeds if desired.
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 minutes until golden on the bottom and the cheese is cooked, serve hot.

name.en: Shakshuka Khaleeji (Gulf-Style Eggs in Tomato Sauce)

en: 2 eggs
2 medium tomatoes, diced
Green bell pepper, diced, and chopped onion
1 crushed garlic clove and ground cumin half a tsp
A pinch of sweet paprika and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper and ragag bread to serve (optional)
Heat the oil in a pan, brown the onion and bell pepper for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt and black pepper, cook 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make two small wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the pan and cook 5-6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft, serve hot with ragag bread if desired.

name.en: Khubz Chapati with Cheese and Herbs

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g and warm water about 40 ml
Low-fat grated cheese 40 g
Chopped spring onion and chopped fresh coriander
A little salt and 1 tsp oil
A pinch of black pepper
Low-fat Greek yogurt 1 tbsp to serve (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water and salt gradually until a soft, cohesive dough forms, let it rest 15 minutes.
Roll into a thin circle, sprinkle the cheese, spring onion, coriander and black pepper over half of it.
Fold the other half over it and press the edges lightly.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat, cook the bread 2-3 minutes on each side until golden and the cheese melts, brush with oil and serve with the yogurt if desired.
Low-fat labneh 150 g
Pitted dates, cut into small pieces, 3 pieces (30 g)
Coarsely chopped almonds 1 tbsp
Honey 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Ragag bread to serve (optional)
Place the labneh in a serving bowl.
Arrange the date pieces and almonds on top.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Serve with ragag bread if desired.
150 g hammour or white fish fillet
100 g cooked basmati rice
1 onion and 2 tomatoes
Machboos spice (cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, loomi)
1 tsp oil, ground dried lime
Season the fish with the spice and a little lime, rest 10 minutes
Bake in the oven 15 minutes at 200°C
Sauté the onion and tomato with the remaining spice
Mix the rice with the sauté and serve with the fish
Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Diced tomato and machboos spice mix 1 tsp (cumin, coriander, cinnamon and ground cardamom)
Light chicken stock 250 ml and salt
Raisins and toasted pine nuts for garnish (optional)
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour, add the tomato, machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice and chicken are fully cooked and absorb the water.
Garnish with raisins and pine nuts if desired and serve hot.
Cracked wheat, soaked overnight, 70 g
Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Water or light vegetable stock 500 ml
Salt and ground cardamom a pinch
Low-fat butter 1 tsp to serve
A pinch of ground cinnamon for garnish (optional)
Place the soaked wheat, chicken, water and salt in a pot, cook over medium heat until it boils, then reduce the heat.
Simmer for about 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until the wheat and chicken are fully cooked and the texture thickens.
Remove the chicken pieces, shred them and return to the pot, mash the mixture with a wooden spoon or whisk until it becomes a smooth, semi-homogeneous texture.
Add the cardamom, pour into a serving bowl, top with the butter and sprinkle with cinnamon if desired, and serve hot.

name.en: Saloona Chicken (Chicken and Vegetable Stew with Rice)

en: Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Carrot and potato, cut into medium pieces, 150 g total
Diced tomato and chopped onion
2 crushed garlic cloves and machboos spice 1 tsp
Light vegetable stock 400 ml and salt
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour, add the tomato, machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the carrot, potato and stock, cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until everything is fully cooked.
Serve hot with the rice.

name.en: Ouzi Rice with Chicken and Nuts

en: Basmati rice 100 g
Cooked, shredded chicken breast 140 g
Chopped onion, browned in a dry pan
Almonds and toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp total for garnish (optional)
Machboos spice half a tsp and ground cardamom a pinch
Light chicken stock 200 ml and salt
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 10-12 minutes until golden.
Cook the rice with the machboos spice, cardamom, salt and stock until fully cooked and absorbing the water.
Add the shredded chicken and browned onion to the rice and stir gently.
Garnish with almonds and pine nuts if desired and serve hot.
Lean lamb, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Diced tomato, zucchini and carrot, cut into medium pieces, 150 g total
Machboos spice 1 tsp and salt
Light meat stock 400 ml
Ragag or whole-wheat bread, cut into pieces, 60 g
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the lamb and stir until it changes colour, add the machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the tomato, zucchini, carrot and stock, cover and simmer 30-35 minutes until the lamb and vegetables are fully cooked.
Arrange the bread pieces in a serving dish, pour the lamb, vegetables and broth over it and serve hot.
Coarse cracked wheat, soaked overnight, 70 g
Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Machboos spice half a tsp and salt
Light chicken stock 450 ml
Crispy fried shallots for garnish (optional)
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken, soaked wheat, machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the stock, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the wheat and chicken are fully cooked and the texture thickens.
Remove the chicken pieces, shred them and return to the pot, mash the mixture lightly with a wooden spoon, garnish with fried shallots if desired and serve hot.

name.en: Fatteh Khaleeji (Bread, Chicken and Yogurt Bowl)

en: Ragag or whole-wheat bread, cut into small pieces and toasted in the oven, 60 g
Cooked, shredded chicken breast 140 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 150 g
1 crushed garlic clove and tahini 1 tsp
Toasted pine nuts 1 tbsp (optional)
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Mix the yogurt with the garlic, tahini and salt until combined.
Arrange the toasted bread pieces in the bottom of a serving dish.
Add the shredded chicken over the bread.
Pour the yogurt sauce over the chicken, sprinkle with black pepper, pine nuts and parsley if desired and serve immediately.
Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
2 onions, thinly sliced and browned
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp for the marinade
Biryani spice 1.5 tsp (cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon and cardamom)
Light chicken stock 250 ml and salt, soaked saffron a pinch
Mix the yogurt with half the biryani spice, marinate the chicken in it and let it sit 20 minutes.
Cook the marinated chicken in a dry pot for 8-10 minutes until cooked.
Add the rice, remaining spice, stock and salt, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and absorbs the water.
Sprinkle with the soaked saffron, garnish with the browned onion and serve hot.
Basmati rice 100 g
Canned chickpeas, drained, 100 g
Carrot and frozen peas, 100 g total
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Machboos spice half a tsp and 1 tsp oil
Light vegetable stock 250 ml and salt
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, carrot, peas, machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice and vegetables are fully cooked and absorb the water.
Drizzle with oil and serve hot.
150 g chicken pieces
Pumpkin, courgette and carrot, chopped
1 onion, 2 tomatoes, puréed
50 g margoog dough sheets (wholewheat flour and water)
Margoog spice, fresh coriander
Simmer the chicken with onion, tomato and spice 20 minutes
Add the pumpkin and carrot, cook 10 minutes
Knead the flour with water and roll into thin sheets
Add the sheets and courgette, cook 10 more minutes with the coriander
100 g yellow lentils
1 carrot, 1 potato, 1 courgette, chopped
1 onion, 1 garlic clove
Saloona spice (turmeric, cumin, dried coriander)
1 tsp oil, puréed tomato
Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil
Add the spice and tomato, stir a minute
Add the lentils and three cups of water, bring to a boil
Add the vegetables and cook 25 minutes until it thickens

name.en: Baked Majboos Laham (Spiced Lamb and Rice)

en: Lean lamb, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Diced tomato and machboos spice mix 1 tsp
1-2 bay leaves and 2 whole cardamom pods (optional)
Light meat stock 250 ml and salt
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the lamb and stir until it changes colour, add the tomato, machboos spice, bay leaves, cardamom and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until the rice and lamb are fully cooked and absorb the water.
Remove the bay leaves and serve hot.
White fish fillet (zubaidi or similar) 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground cumin, ground coriander and turmeric a pinch, half a tsp each
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Chopped fresh coriander for garnish
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the fish with it and let it sit 15-20 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes until fully cooked, garnish with fresh coriander and serve with the rice.
Hammour or similar fish fillet 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Ground cumin, ground coriander and paprika half a tsp each
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Chopped fresh coriander for garnish
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the fish with it and let it sit 15-20 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes until fully cooked, garnish with fresh coriander and serve with the rice.
Chicken breast, cut into large pieces, 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Diced tomato and kabsa spice mix 1.5 tsp (cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom and ground cloves)
Light chicken stock 250 ml and salt
Raisins and toasted pine nuts for garnish (optional)
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir until it changes colour, add the tomato, kabsa spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice and chicken are fully cooked and absorb the water.
Garnish with raisins and pine nuts if desired and serve hot.
Peeled medium shrimp 140 g
Basmati rice 100 g
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Diced tomato and machboos spice mix 1 tsp
Light fish or vegetable stock 250 ml and salt
Chopped fresh coriander for garnish
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato, machboos spice and salt, stir for two minutes.
Add the rice and stock, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the shrimp on top of the rice without stirring, cover and cook another 5-7 minutes until the shrimp and rice are fully cooked, garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

name.en: Baked Whole Spice Chicken with Rice

en: Skinless chicken thighs 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 2 tbsp
Machboos spice 1 tsp and low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp for the marinade
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Chopped parsley for garnish
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, machboos spice, yogurt, salt and black pepper to make the marinade.
Rub the chicken thoroughly with it and let it sit at least 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden on the outside, garnish with parsley and serve with the rice.

name.en: Grilled Kofta with Tahini Sauce and Rice

en: Lean minced beef 140 g
Grated onion and chopped parsley
Machboos spice half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Tahini 2 tbsp and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Warm water about 80 ml and 1 crushed garlic clove for the sauce
Cooked basmati rice 110 g
Knead the minced beef thoroughly with the grated onion, parsley, machboos spice, salt and black pepper until it binds together.
Shape into long fingers around wooden skewers soaked in water.
Grill under the broiler or in a 220°C oven for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked.
Mix the tahini, lemon juice and garlic with the warm water gradually until you get a smooth sauce, pour over the kofta and serve with the rice.

name.en: Baked Fish Sayadieh Khaleeji (Spiced Fish and Rice with Caramelized Onions)

en: White fish fillet 140 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
2 crushed garlic cloves and ground cumin 1 tsp
Ground coriander half a tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Basmati rice 100 g and light fish or vegetable stock 200 ml
Lemon juice, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion in a dry pan over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, stirring, until it turns dark and sweet.
Divide the browned onion in half, mash one half and set aside for garnish.
Cook the rice with half the mashed onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon and stock until fully cooked.
Season the fish with salt, black pepper and lemon juice, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, serve over the rice and garnish with the remaining browned onion.

name.en: Thin bread with labneh and thyme

en: 1 thin rakak flatbread
50 g low-fat labneh
1 tsp chopped fresh thyme
1 tsp olive oil
Cucumber slices to serve
Spread the labneh over the flatbread
Sprinkle the thyme and oil on top
Roll it up tightly
Cut into pieces and serve with cucumber
1 black tea bag
150 ml low-fat milk
2 crushed cardamom pods
1 tsp honey
A small piece of ginger (optional)
Boil water with the tea, cardamom and ginger for 2 minutes
Add the milk and bring back to a boil
Lower the heat and let it steep 3 minutes
Strain into a cup and sweeten with the honey
Lean minced beef 90 g
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Machboos spice half a tsp and chopped fresh coriander
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing, salt and black pepper
A little lemon juice (optional)
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Add the minced beef and stir until fully cooked, add the machboos spice, coriander, salt, black pepper and lemon juice if desired.
Cut each pastry sheet in half, place a spoonful of filling on each half and fold into a triangle, press the edges to seal.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg, and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g and water about 70 ml
Low-fat grated cheese 40 g
Chopped spring onion and a pinch of chopped fresh mint
A little salt and a pinch of ground cumin
1 tsp oil
Black pepper
Mix the flour with the water gradually until a very thin, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour a very thin layer of batter to cover the base.
Cook for a minute until the edges dry, sprinkle the cheese, spring onion, mint, salt, cumin and black pepper over half of it.
Fold the other half over it, press gently and cook another minute on both sides until the cheese melts, serve hot.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g and water about 70 ml
Cooked lean minced beef 70 g
Chopped onion and machboos spice half a tsp
A little salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour with the water gradually until a very thin, lump-free liquid batter forms.
Mix the cooked meat with the onion, spice, salt and black pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour a very thin layer of batter to cover the base, cook for a minute until the edges dry.
Spread the meat filling over half of it, fold the other half over it, press gently and cook another minute on both sides, cut and garnish with parsley if desired and serve hot.
Canned chickpeas, drained and dried well, 200 g
1 tsp olive oil
Mixed spice (Gulf baharat) 1 tbsp
A little salt
A little lemon juice after roasting
A pinch of cayenne pepper (optional)
Dry the chickpeas thoroughly with a paper towel to remove as much moisture as possible.
Mix them with the oil, spice mix and salt.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until fully crisp, sprinkle with lemon juice and cayenne pepper if desired after removing and serve once slightly cooled.
Low-fat cottage cheese 80 g
Low-fat grated mozzarella 30 g
Chopped spring onion and a pinch of chopped fresh mint
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing, salt and black pepper
Nigella seeds a pinch for garnish (optional)
Mix the cottage cheese and mozzarella with the spring onion, mint, salt and black pepper until combined.
Cut each pastry sheet in half, place a spoonful of filling on each half and fold into a triangle, press the edges to seal.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg, sprinkle with nigella seeds if desired.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.

name.en: Stuffed Dates with Walnuts and Tahini

en: Large pitted dates, 8 pieces (80 g)
Coarsely chopped walnuts 2 tbsp
Tahini 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Toasted sesame seeds 1 tsp for garnish (optional)
A pinch of salt
Mix the chopped walnuts with the tahini, cinnamon and a pinch of salt until the texture holds together slightly.
Open each date on one side without separating it completely.
Fill each date with a small spoonful of the walnut and tahini mixture.
Arrange on a serving plate, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds if desired and serve at room temperature.
Boiled and mashed potato 80 g
Cooked carrot and frozen peas, 50 g total
A pinch of ground cumin and chopped fresh coriander
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheets, 4 pieces (60 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing, salt and black pepper
A little lemon juice
Mix the mashed potato with the carrot, peas, cumin, coriander, lemon juice, salt and black pepper until combined.
Cut each pastry sheet in half, place a spoonful of filling on each half and fold into a triangle, press the edges to seal.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Raw almonds 15 g
Raw walnuts 15 g
Raw cashews 10 g
1 tsp olive oil
Mixed spice (Gulf baharat) half a tsp
A little salt
Mix the almonds, walnuts and cashews with the oil, spice mix and salt until evenly coated.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and fragrant.
Let cool completely before serving to become crisp.
250 ml low-fat milk
2 tbsp cornstarch
Saffron threads, steeped
1 tsp sugar or honey
Crushed almonds and pistachios to garnish
Dissolve the cornstarch in a quarter cup of cold milk
Heat the rest of the milk with the saffron and sugar
Add the cornstarch mix and stir on low heat until it thickens
Pour into cups, chill 2 hours and top with the nuts
Half cup wholewheat flour
Half tsp instant yeast
1 tsp ground cardamom
A light spray of olive oil for the tray
2 tbsp date syrup to serve
Mix the flour, yeast and cardamom with warm water into a soft dough
Let it rest 45 minutes in a warm place
Shape small balls on an oiled tray
Bake 15 minutes at 190°C and serve with the syrup
Semolina 50 g
Pitted dates, chopped, 60 g
Water 150 ml and low-fat butter 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cardamom and a pinch of saffron (optional)
A pinch of ground cinnamon for garnish
Coarsely chopped walnuts 1 tsp for garnish (optional)
Heat the butter in a small pot over medium heat, add the semolina and toast it for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and slightly golden.
Gradually add the water while stirring quickly to avoid lumps.
Add the chopped dates, cardamom and saffron if desired, cook 5-7 minutes over low heat, stirring, until the texture thickens and the dates partially dissolve.
Pour into serving bowls, sprinkle with cinnamon and walnuts if desired, and serve warm.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Warm water about 50 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Brown sugar 1 tsp and saffron soaked in a spoon of warm water
A pinch of ground cardamom
1 tsp oil for the batter
Honey 2 tbsp to serve
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast, brown sugar, soaked saffron, cardamom and oil gradually until a thick, sticky batter forms.
Let it rest 30-40 minutes until roughly doubled in size.
Use two spoons to shape small balls of the batter and place on a lined tray with space between them.
Bake at 220°C for 14-16 minutes, turning halfway, until golden, pour honey over them while hot and serve immediately.

name.en: Khaleeji Umm Ali (Gulf Bread Pudding with Nuts and Saffron)

en: Ragag bread or whole-wheat toast, cut into small pieces, 40 g
Low-fat milk 250 ml
Brown sugar 15 g and saffron soaked in a spoon of warm water
A pinch of ground cardamom
Almonds and walnuts, coarsely chopped, 1 tbsp total for garnish
Raisins 1 tsp for garnish (optional)
Arrange the bread pieces in a small oven-safe dish.
Heat the milk with the brown sugar, soaked saffron and cardamom in a small pot until nearly boiling.
Pour the milk over the bread and let it sit 5 minutes to absorb.
Sprinkle with almonds, walnuts and raisins if desired, bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until the top is golden, and serve warm.
Sago (tapioca pearls) 40 g
Low-fat milk 300 ml
Brown sugar 20 g
Rosewater 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cardamom
Coarsely chopped pistachios for garnish (optional)
Soak the sago in warm water for 15-20 minutes until it starts to soften, drain.
Place it in a small oven-safe dish, add the milk, brown sugar and cardamom.
Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until the sago fully absorbs the milk and becomes translucent and creamy, add the rosewater, sprinkle with pistachios if desired and serve warm or cold.

name.en: Gulf Halwa (Sweet Jelly Dessert with Nuts and Saffron)

en: Cornflour 40 g
Water 250 ml
Brown sugar 45 g
Saffron soaked in a spoon of warm water and ground cardamom a pinch
1 tsp low-fat butter
Almonds and pistachios, coarsely chopped, 1 tbsp total for garnish
Dissolve the cornflour in a quarter cup of cold water until smooth without lumps.
Heat the remaining water with the brown sugar in a small pot until nearly boiling.
Gradually stir in the cornflour mixture, stirring constantly, cook 7-9 minutes over medium-low heat until the texture becomes thick, translucent and semi-gelatinous.
Add the saffron, cardamom and butter, pour into a small greased tin, sprinkle with almonds and pistachios, let it chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours before slicing and serving.
Whole-wheat flour 70 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Brown sugar 30 g and 1 egg
Saffron soaked in a spoon of warm water and ground cardamom a pinch
Baking powder half a tsp
Toasted sesame seeds 1 tsp for garnish
Mix the melted butter with the brown sugar and egg until well combined.
Add the soaked saffron, cardamom, baking powder and flour gradually and mix until a smooth cake batter forms.
Pour into a small greased tin, sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until the centre is cooked and the top is golden, let cool slightly before slicing and serving.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Melted low-fat butter 2 tbsp
Warm water about 20 ml and a pinch of instant yeast
Pitted dates, mashed, 50 g for the filling
A pinch of ground cardamom and a pinch of ground cinnamon for the filling
A pinch of sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour with the melted butter until fully absorbed, gradually add the warm water and yeast and knead until a soft, cohesive dough forms, let it rest 30 minutes.
Mix the mashed dates with the cardamom and cinnamon for the filling.
Shape the dough into small balls, press each ball to form a hollow, fill with dates and seal, flatten slightly.
Arrange on a lined tray, sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired, bake at 180°C for 16-18 minutes until golden on the bottom.
Well-cooked white rice 50 g
Low-fat milk 300 ml
Brown sugar 25 g
Saffron soaked in a spoon of warm water and ground cardamom a pinch
Coarsely chopped almonds 1 tsp for garnish
A pinch of ground cinnamon for garnish (optional)
Place the cooked rice with the milk and brown sugar in a small pot over medium heat.
Cook 12-15 minutes, stirring constantly, until the texture thickens and becomes creamy.
Add the soaked saffron and cardamom, cook 2 more minutes.
Pour into serving bowls, sprinkle with almonds and cinnamon if desired, and serve warm or cold.
